drafts.text:
HOOK
The Federal Reserve is about to reveal what really happened behind closed doors.
[ON SCREEN: Fed building graphic with "FOMC Minutes"]

WHAT IT IS
The US FOMC Minutes drop today at 14:00 ET, giving traders a detailed look inside the central bank's latest policy debate.
[ON SCREEN: Text "FOMC Minutes: 14:00 ET"]

WHY IT MATTERS
This release can spark sharp swings across the US Dollar Index, EUR/USD, Gold, and the S&P 500. Active traders will comb through the text to see how divided policymakers were on interest rate cuts and economic growth.
[ON SCREEN: Tickers: DXY, EUR/USD, XAU/USD, S&P 500]

WHAT TO WATCH
If the tone leans hawkish, showing persistent inflation worries, the dollar could rally while stocks and Gold pull back. On the other hand, any focus on labor market softness could weaken the dollar and lift equities.
[ON SCREEN: Graphic comparing hawkish vs dovish market reactions]

CLOSE
Catch the full breakdown on FXEmpire.
[ON SCREEN: FXEmpire logo and website URL]

HOOK
Is the American consumer finally hitting the brakes?
[ON SCREEN: Tiger to camera with US consumer graphic]

WHAT IT IS
At 08:30 ET, we get the US Retail Sales report for Oct. The consensus expects 0%, down from 0.8% last month.
[ON SCREEN: Retail Sales forecast 0% vs previous 0.8%]

WHY IT MATTERS
Consumer spending drives most of the US economy. That makes this a crucial catalyst for the US Dollar Index, EUR/USD, and the S&P 500. When shoppers pull back or keep spending, interest rate expectations can shift immediately.
[ON SCREEN: Ticker symbols: US Dollar Index, EUR/USD, S&P 500]

WHAT TO WATCH
If the number lands well above 0%, it signals resilience. That could lift the greenback and pressure EUR/USD. But if spending comes in below expectations, growth worries could weigh on equities while softening the dollar.

drafts.text:
HOOK
UK employment data is about to hit the tape, and currency traders need to pay attention.
[ON SCREEN: GBP/USD ticker and chart]

WHAT IT IS
The UK Unemployment Rate for Sep drops at 02:00 ET. Markets are looking for 4.9%, up from 4.7% in the previous reading.
[ON SCREEN: "Forecast: 4.9% | Previous: 4.7%"]

WHY IT MATTERS
This release is critical for the Bank of England's rate path. Any sign of a softening job market can quickly influence the British pound against the dollar and euro, while also shifting momentum in the FTSE 100.
[ON SCREEN: Split screen showing GBP/USD, EUR/GBP, and FTSE 100]

WHAT TO WATCH
If the reading lands above 4.9%, it could signal rising labor market slack and pressure sterling. But an unexpected drop below 4.9% might support the pound as traders trim rate cut expectations.
[ON SCREEN: Text graphic "Above 4.9%: Pressure on GBP | Below 4.9%: Support for GBP"]

CLOSE
Get the full breakdown on FXEmpire.
[ON SCREEN: FXEmpire logo and website URL]
